steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: Copland's style features open harmonies (wide-spaced chords), sparse textures, and folk-derived melodies — his Americana sound defines mid-20th century US orchestral music. | Key Fact: British composers combined pastoral tradition with modernism: Britten's dramatic orchestration, Tavener's spiritual minimalism, Maxwell-Davies's folk-modernist fusion. | Key Fact: Fanfare for the Common Man uses open fifths, brass sonority and slow-building dynamics to create monumental, democratic grandeur. | Key Fact: Britten's Young Person's Guide shows orchestral variation technique — each instrument family is showcased through Purcell-based variations.

steps.title: Lesson 3: Application
steps.body: Describe how copland and british orchestral music are used in a piece of music you have studied. Explain the effect in each case. | How could you use copland and british orchestral music in your own composition or performance? Explain your choices.
